brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#0 (hex-acc-keyhole, Keyhole hanger) is seated on the full base piece:0,0,0 slot 0. check_build reports meshClash clear. Wall screws and the hanging itself are not something the configurator can verify.

requirements.requirement: With hooks for small hand tools
requirements.evidence: Three hex-acc-hook hook plates (accessory:0#0,0#1, 0#2, 0#3) each carry two hooks, on slots 1-3 of the same base. The hook plates offer mounts only for a cable coil, gaffer tape roll or FPV goggles; the configurator refuses a screwdriver or hex key set on them, and a gaffer tape roll hangs 25 mm through the bench, so no tools were placed. The hooks exist, but I could not show small hand tools hanging on them.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability for wall use (load, strength, weather)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot verify the printed material's load rating or durability for holding tools.

finish.summary: Built a single full hex base with one keyhole hanger on one face, three hook plates on three other faces, and a solid cap on the remaining open face. check_build is clear (meshClash clear, no errors; one info note about one open face). The hooks are real parts, but the configurator only lets wall hooks carry cable coils, gaffer tape or FPV goggles, so I could not demonstrate hand tools on them. The keyhole hanger's orientation to the wall is not confirmed by the tool, and load/material suitability is not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
